messages:
ashley: quick pulse check — after yesterday's routing tweak i see odd batch shapes on p3 pools, small 1-2 token microbatches spiking latency. attaching quick notes
cheng: saw that too. looks correlated with new multi-variant fallback policy that prefers lower-cost variants. when compatset expands, batches fragment.
samir: short version: compatset fanout -> smaller compat buckets -> less coalescing -> lower GPU throughput. also kv-cache hitrate dropped ~6% on the same traffic replay.
ashley: thanks. can someone share the profiler flame for a sample request? wondering if kernel selection is bouncing between int8 and fp16 pathways which could cause jitter.
cheng: pasted a trimmed trace: ```
[TRACE] seq=512 model=v2a variant=quant8 fallback=enabled
kernel_load: conv+fused_attn (0.43ms)
kv_lookup: hit=false
batch_form: size=2 wait=12ms
kernel_exec: int8_path (1.9ms)
kernel_exec: fp16_path (2.0ms)
```
samir: yep, that's the problem — we end up doing both code paths because the compatset maps similar arch models with different quantization. kernel selector currently chooses per-request, not per-batch.
ashley: ops, can we run a targeted replay with stable kernel affinity (force per-batch kernel binding) + token_budget=256 and compare? want to see batching recovery and kv-hit delta.
ops: running now on canary pool. replay id: r-21512-kvprobe. ETA ~7m. infra-bot: replay started on pool-us-east-1-p3. canary=10 nodes.
cheng: also tweak queue policy to prefer age-based merging over compat-first for this run. i suspect compat-first is over-fragmenting when token windows are tiny.
samir: to add: if kv-hitrate stays low, that suggests our prefix caching is getting invalidated by variant fallbacks. we should instrument cache keys to include variant id or a compatibility mask.
ashley: agree. short-term mitigation: keep fallback on but unify kernel path selection to batch-level and enforce cache key normalization. long-term: support compat-aware cache sharding and merge heuristics that consider expected kernel path.
ops: replay finished. quick metrics: median latency down 18% with per-batch kernel binding, p99 down 12%. kv-hitrate improved +4% vs baseline. batch size mean increased from 1.9 -> 3.6.
samir: promising. any regressions?
ops: one perf regression surfaced for long sequences (>2048) where forcing int8 for the batch caused occasional accuracy regressions in evals. not catastrophic but flagged by quality tests.
cheng: put a guard: if any request in batch > 2048 keep fp16 for whole batch. that keeps latency wins for most traffic and avoids quality regressions.
ashley: action items: 1) samir to PR kernel-selector change to batch affinity + guard for long sequences (owners: samir) 2) cheng to prototype cache-key normalization + instrument variant tag (owners: cheng) 3) ops to run 48h canary with new queue policy and token_budget presets (owners: ops) 4) infra-bot to add automated replay job for any compatset change.
samir: i'll open PR and include perf bench numbers and the p99/p50 delta.
cheng: i'll add telemetry fields: compatset_id, kernel_path, cache_key_norm in request logs.
ashley: great. keep notes here. left a quick :thumbsup: on the canary results. we'll roll to staging after PR review and a green 48h canary.
